Instruction: Always sync updated Next.js skills and any specifically modified skill in '.agents/skills/' directly to 'd:/Scripts/Obsidian/skills/' without blind bulk copying of all skills - ensure customized/updated skills are centrally mirrored in the Obsidian vault.
Why: user preference: keep Next.js and modified skills synced to Obsidian knowledge base

Instruction: Always invoke and scan '.agents/skills/self-repair' and load '.agents/autofix.json' at session start and before executing any task - ensure active learned rules and constraints are always enforced.
Why: user explicit instruction to invoke self-repair every time

Instruction: In dev setup skills and automation workflows, never create dummy or sample test files in the project workspace; provide sample test code strictly as reference snippets in documentation and skills.
Why: user preference: keep project clean of dummy/sample test files during initial setup

Instruction: Configure git pre-push hooks to execute both Jest unit tests and Playwright E2E tests (e.g., 'pnpm run test:all') to guarantee full test suite validation before pushing code.
Why: user requirement: verify both unit and E2E test suites before git push

Instruction: In Next.js i18n configuration, the translation dictionaries directory is 'messages' at the project root (e.g. 'messages/en.json', 'messages/fa.json'), not 'app/dictionaries'.
Why: user explicit correction: next-intl standard root messages directory convention

Instruction: Do not configure or generate Docker development environments (no Dockerfile.dev or dev compose watch service) - configure Docker strictly for standalone production builds (Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml for production standalone, .dockerignore, and next.config standalone output).
Why: user explicit preference: user runs dev server locally without docker and only wants Docker for production containerization

Instruction: In Docker containerization setup, always name the Docker Compose configuration file 'docker-compose.yml' (not 'compose.yaml').
Why: user explicit preference: standard docker-compose.yml naming convention

Instruction: In multi-architecture Docker container workflows (AMD64 & ARM64), build natively on separate dedicated runner machines in matrix jobs without using QEMU emulation (docker/setup-qemu-action).
Why: user explicit preference: build multi-arch container images natively across separate machines without QEMU emulation

Instruction: In GitHub Actions CI/CD and Release Please workflows, configure concurrency 'cancel-in-progress: false' to ensure ongoing workflow runs and release builds on main are never cancelled when new commits are pushed.
Why: user explicit preference: prevent workflow runs and release builds from being cancelled by subsequent commits

Instruction: In GitHub Actions container build workflows (GHCR/Docker), always lowercase the repository name (e.g. using 'tr [:upper:] [:lower:]' into an IMAGE_NAME environment variable) because Docker OCI naming specifications strictly forbid uppercase characters.
Why: fix failure: Docker buildx failed with 'repository name must be lowercase' when repository owner/name contains uppercase characters

Instruction: Create custom React UI components (including JSX wrappers like Link) in separate .tsx files under the components directory (e.g. 'app/components/Link.tsx') and keep navigation helper configuration files like 'i18n/navigation.ts' pure TypeScript without JSX.
Why: user explicit correction: create the Link component in a separate file in @components

Instruction: Never chain multiple commands using '&&', '||', or ';' on a single line; execute terminal commands individually as discrete single operations. When running inspection commands like 'git diff' or 'git status', avoid appending unnecessary specific path arguments unless specifically required so commands match user-configured custom permissions and allowlists.
Why: user requirement: compound one-liner commands and granular arguments break Antigravity custom permissions and command allowlists

Instruction: Antigravity (AG) only discovers and loads MCP servers that are configured globally on the host system (e.g. '~/.gemini/antigravity/mcp_config.json' and '~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json'). When setting up or updating MCP servers (such as 'next-devtools' or 'playwright'), always configure them for BOTH the workspace (e.g. 'mcp.json', '.vscode/mcp.json', or '.agents/plugins/workspace-tools/mcp_config.json') AND globally for AG on the host system.
Why: user explicit correction: AG only recognizes MCP servers configured globally on the host system, so both workspace and global AG configurations must always be configured

Instruction: When setting up MCP servers globally on the host system, configure them strictly for Google Antigravity / AGY only ('~/.gemini/antigravity/mcp_config.json' and '~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json'). Do NOT configure or register MCP servers globally for other coding agents (e.g., Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, Cline).
Why: user explicit requirement: setup MCP servers globally for AGY only, not for other coding agents

Instruction: When executing cross-directory file synchronization, copy operations, or filesystem tasks on Windows, invoke PowerShell ('powershell -Command ...') instead of writing and running ad-hoc Python scratch scripts.
Why: user explicit correction and preference: use powershell for file operations

Instruction: In the 'nextjs-plan' skill and 'docs/plan.md', Step 1 must grill the user on what pages the web app needs, followed by what sections and components each page requires; in 'docs/plan.md', outline every page as a checklist item with all of its components as nested sub-checklists, where a page is ticked off only when all its components are designed.
Why: user explicit requirement: grill on pages then sections, and outline pages with component sub-checklists ticked off when all components are designed

Instruction: In Storybook stories created for components, write comprehensive structured markdown documentation in 'parameters.docs.description.component' and export strictly four story variants: 'Light' (configured with light theme and dedicated light background container), 'Dark' (configured with dark theme and dedicated dark background container), 'SkeletonLight' (skeleton fallback configured with light theme and dedicated light background container), and 'SkeletonDark' (skeleton fallback configured with dark theme and dedicated dark background container) so both light and dark variants of the component and its skeleton are immediately visible side-by-side with proper contrast on Storybook Docs pages. All Storybook preview wrappers, backgrounds, and story decorators MUST strictly use the production semantic theme tokens from 'app/globals.css' ('bg-background', 'text-foreground', 'border-border', 'text-muted-foreground', etc.) with scoped '.light' and '.dark' classes; hardcoding custom arbitrary styles or hex/palette colors (such as '#FAFAFA', '#050505', 'border-zinc-*') in Storybook is strictly prohibited.
Why: user explicit requirement: use production theme tokens for component creation and Storybook backgrounds without hardcoding custom styles, write docs for storybook, and display both light and dark variants of the component and skeleton with high contrast on Docs pages

Instruction: In the '/nextjs-create-component' workflow, the verification gate in Step 7 MUST physically execute Storybook verification tests (both smoke/indexing test via 'pnpm run storybook:smoke' or 'storybook dev --smoke-test' and static production build via 'pnpm run build-storybook') alongside baseline and adversarial test suites to ensure zero syntax errors, AST parsing breaks, or bundle failures before declaring completion.
Why: user explicit requirement: add the story book test to verification gate of /nextjs-create-component

Instruction: When using the 'codebase-memory-mcp' code intelligence server, always maintain a root '.cbmignore' file excluding high-churn files ('.agents/', 'docs/', build caches, test reports, and '.codebase-memory/') and configure 'auto_watch = false' (via 'codebase-memory-mcp config set auto_watch false') to prevent system stutters and constant background re-indexing during file editing.
Why: diagnosed performance issue: codebase-memory background git watcher triggers reindexing and zstd artifact rewrites on every save, causing system stutters

Instruction: Always invoke and apply '.agents/skills/codebase-memory' before searching, exploring, reading code, or assessing change impact. Because background watcher re-indexing is disabled ('auto_watch = false') to prevent system stutters, the agent MUST always ensure graph freshness by checking 'index_status' or executing 'index_repository' (with mode='fast' or 'moderate') before issuing search queries, and always prioritize codebase-memory graph tools ('search_graph', 'trace_path', 'get_code_snippet', 'detect_changes') over naive text grep or full-file reading.
Why: user explicit requirement: create a skill that the agent always invokes and configures agent to use codebase memory mcp to search the codebase and always indexes codebase first since on-watch indexing is disabled

Instruction: In Antigravity global MCP configurations ('~/.gemini/antigravity/mcp_config.json' and '~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json'), 'agy.exe' does not respect '"disabled": true' inside the 'mcpServers' object and will still launch the child processes. To properly disable an MCP server, move it completely out of 'mcpServers' (e.g., into a separate '_disabledMcpServers' object).
Why: diagnosed behavior: agy launches all commands defined under mcpServers regardless of disabled flag

Instruction: In the SiteNavbar component, design specifications, and preview artifacts, do not render availability/status badges or version tags in the brand identity lockup; keep the brand lockup clean with the emblem, brand title, and optional systems role.
Why: user explicit instruction: remove the availability badge and version in site navbar

Instruction: In navigation components (SiteNavbar, MobileNavDrawer), design specifications, and preview artifacts, do not render 'COCKPIT TOPOLOGY', uptime badges (such as '99.9%'), or availability/status badges; keep the brand lockup and navigation links clean without extraneous telemetry badges.
Why: user explicit instruction: remove cockpit topology, uptime, and availability badge

Instruction: NEVER use 'read_url_content' to download binary files (images, raw HTML exports, or any non-text binary). It is a text-only fetcher that corrupts binary data and mangles file content. Always use 'run_command' with PowerShell 'Invoke-WebRequest -Uri <url> -OutFile <path>' to download any binary or raw file directly to disk.
Why: diagnosed mistake: used read_url_content to download Stitch JPG and HTML files — JPGs were corrupted (unreadable), HTML was not the raw source. Fix: always use Invoke-WebRequest for binary downloads.
